chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a woman becomes a Muslim and her husband remains upon other than Islam, separation is effected between them.

He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who emigrated and left his wife among the Polytheists, then she joined him afterwards. Can he retain her under the first marriage, or does her bond of marriage cease? He (peace be upon him) said: No, he retains her and she is his wife.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage bond if a Muslim woman reunites with her polytheist husband after initial separation due to her conversion?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'faskh' (automatic separation) in mixed-faith marriages, specifically addressing the status of the marital bond when a Muslim woman remains with her non-Muslim husband who has not yet converted. It establishes that if she later reunites with him, the original nikah is reinstated without requiring a new contract, a ruling derived from the principle that the initial separation was conditional upon her conversion status. This reflects the Shia scholarly view on the continuity of marital ties in cases of religious disparity.
